free_tier.stated: Free premium link generator with a per-host daily traffic allowance; the page's own counter reads 'Files Per Day: 0 / 5'.
free_tier.notes: Five files per day for an anonymous caller. The byte allowance is separate and per host, not per account.

per_object_cap.stated: not stated on the page read; the listed limits are daily byte totals per host, not a single-file cap
per_object_cap.notes: A per-object cap would have to be read from a host-specific generator page; none was opened.

retention.stated: not applicable: the service generates a download link and does not offer storage

egress.terms: The link streams from Leechall's own servers, so the byte counter that binds is Leechall's, per host, per day. The page lists caps such as 'extmatrix.com 0 B / 6 GB /d', '1fichier.com 0 B / 8 GB /d', 'mega.nz 0 B / 1 GB /d', 'isra.cloud 0 B / 650 MB /d', 'emload.com 0 B / 250 MB /d'.
egress.free_allowance: per-host daily totals: extmatrix 6 GB/d, 1fichier 8 GB/d, mega.nz 1 GB/d, alfafile 1 GB/d, filestore.to 5 GB/d, tezfiles 800 MB/d, hitfile 650 MB/d, isra.cloud 650 MB/d, chomikuj.pl 350 MB/d, emload 250 MB/d

interface_detail: A web form: paste a host URL, receive a generated link. The only other channel the page offers is a Telegram channel for status (t.me/leechallcom). No API, CLI or rclone backend was found.
tooling: none today: browser form only. A wrapper would have to drive the form or reverse its request shape; that is a tooling gap, not a verdict.
chaining: Covers the small set of hosts a debrid subscription does not: extmatrix, isra.cloud, emload, chomikuj.pl. At 250 MB/day on emload and 650 MB/day on isra it moves a few hundred megabytes a day, so it supplements a paid debrid rather than replacing one.

limits.value: 5 files per day (page counter 'Files Per Day: 0 / 5')
per-host daily caps, 250 MB/day (emload) to 8 GB/day (1fichier)

limits_note: A host not on the list cannot be fetched at all.
binding_note: The daily byte ceiling on each host is what fails first.

identity_cost.detail: The generator ran with no account on the page read; the page prints a usage counter against the caller's network ('Your IP: ...', 'You Used: 0 B'), so the identity it bills is the egress address, not a login.

reliability_note: When a host's daily allowance is exhausted the generator still answers and the link fails at download; the counter is against the caller's IP, so a shared or changing egress address changes the allowance.
confidence_note: Read on the live site. A generated link that completes a download would raise this to measured; that needs a target URL on a supported host.

evidence.proved: 'Files Per Day: 0 / 5', the per-host daily table (extmatrix 6 GB/d, 1fichier 8 GB/d, isra.cloud 650 MB/d, emload 250 MB/d), and the 59-host supported list
the same operator sells a paid ad-free service from $2.99, which fixes leechall.com's free tier in the product line

notes: The per-host caps are the useful artefact: they are a third-party statement of what each host lets a leecher pull per day, which is the number the filehost's own pages rarely publish.
